gen-dafont-neon-fs-amulya: Every Neon letter carries one unbroken line width, tall and stamped-looking, glowing against the lower, moodier build of Amulya. Amulya's plain sans curves keep their gaps generous.
gen-dafont-neon-fs-chillax: Glow with a stamped edge. Neon stands tall and uninterrupted, while Chillax drops lower and loosens up, its pen-lifted curves left pleasantly unfinished like spaghetti on a plate.
gen-dafont-neon-fs-roundo: Neon holds one uninterrupted line width across every tall, stamped-looking letter, and its spacing stays open throughout. Roundo follows with tidy arches and unclogged small counters, leaving the big, short lines to Neon.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-quando: Neon draws every curve with a flat, unswelling line, glowing and tall like stamped metal type. And Quando, a bookish text serif with sparse spacing, is the one that settles into the paragraphs.
gen-dafont-neon-space-grotesk: Space Grotesk reads as a plain sans whose counters breathe, built from a constant ribbon of line. Neon takes the tall, glowing display work, while Space Grotesk stays lower.
gen-dafont-neuropol-fs-epilogue: Neuropol feels digital and futuristic, its channels slim and its outlines single-weight. Epilogue loosens it, with curvy, open plain sans letters and stubby ascender tips under the closed, tight heading.
gen-dafont-neuropol-fs-public-sans: A slim channel opens each c in Neuropol, and the single-weight outline gives it a digital, futuristic edge. Public Sans counters with hefty, broad-countered sans-serif letters.
gen-dafont-neuropolitical-fs-amulya: Letters pulled apart, glowing. Neuropolitical runs one steady stroke through every tall glyph, while Amulya sits lower with generous gaps in its sans-serif curves, and that contrast is the pair's hook.
gen-dafont-neuropolitical-fs-chillax: Chillax reads loose and casual, its sans-serif line like spaghetti with pen-lifted curves left unfinished in each loop. Neuropolitical's rigid, neon-tube strokes make the relaxed body feel even looser.
gen-dafont-neuropolitical-fs-synonym: Neuropolitical looks pulled apart, letter by letter, with big open counters. Synonym lays down a plain stripe of ink in sans-serif forms, so a longer passage should read cleanly, with generous openings in every curve.
